newsitem.title: USA: San Franciscans oppose paying for stadium - poll.
newsitem.headline: San Franciscans oppose paying for stadium - poll.

text.p: Most San Francisco voters would oppose the use of public funds for a new football stadium for the National Football League's 49ers, according to a poll published on Monday.
Just 21 percent of voters, surveyed October 23-24, said "yes" when asked if the city should "contribute significantly" to a new 49ers stadium, the San Francisco Examiner newspaper poll found.

Sixty-eight percent of the respondents said they did not support the use of public funds, while 11 percent were undecided, according to the poll by Mason-Dixon Political/Media Research for the Examiner.

The San Francisco 49ers team, which has wanted to move out of aging Candlestick Park for years, recently proposed a new 74,000-seat stadium expected to cost about $250 million. Officials with the team said they wanted to develop a public-private partnership to finance the facility.
A San Francisco Chronicle poll published in late October showed that only 28 percent of city voters would say "yes" to building a new 49ers stadium financed in part by public funds.
